newsitem.title: GERMANY: Pizza fills a knead in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Pizza fills a knead in Europe.

text.p: It's the tomato sauce, dough and mozzarella mania that keeps millions from going hungry at night.
Pizza, in all its deliverable, take-out and frozen forms, was elevated to an art form at a pizza convention that was held recently in Berlin.

"It is a world-wide phenomenon," said Brigitte Heimann, organiser of PizzaTec, Europe's first pizza convention that opened with 88 exhibitors from 12 countries. Berlin was the likely choice for the expo, being Germany's pizza capital with 1,000 pizzerias and 850,000 pizzas consumed each day.

"It is the most successful ethnic dish ever," she added, while eating a slice topped with curried chicken and pineapple. "It's tasty, it's cheap -- which is particularly attractive for younger people -- and it's available everywhere."
Pizza sales in Germany grew by 13 percent between 1995 and 1996 to 45,000 tons per year, she said, making the country one of the world's leading consumers.
Frozen pizzas alone accounted for over $300 million in sales in Germany during the first half of 1996, around 60 percent of which are bought by single and two-person households.

Heimann said she brought the professionals' pizza fair to Berlin to help the favourite dish conquer new markets in Eastern Europe and Asia. The pizza convention also aims to spread the word on technological advancements.

"I've had calls from Russians, Koreans, Japanese, Polish, Indians and South Americans who want to attend the convention," Heimann said. "They are very interested but don't yet have the know-how to get pizza businesses off the ground."
The convention hall booths boasted new models of cardbord boxes, brick ovens, and preparation tables, along with new ideas like an aerosol garlic and olive oil spray.
The cyber-age has also reached the pizza industry, with two German firms offering nationwide menu listings and an online order service which hooks up hungry surfers with their favourite parlour.
Heimann commission a "Pizze d'arte team" to create spoofs on famous works by Dali, Picasso and Mondrian painted on dough with tomato sauce, cheese and olives.
Photos of the masterpieces are available for "avant garde" pizzerias, according to Heimann, for $400 each.
